title: Dedicated first-run: capacity estimator & SLA compare visuals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create a set of onboarding visuals and annotated screenshots for the Dedicated first-run flow that help engineers and product leads quickly configure capacity, understand autoscaling behavior, and choose an SLA tier. This ticket covers the capacity estimator interactive mockups (desktop + mobile), an SLA comparison blade that visualizes cost vs latency/risk, and an animated autoscale simulation GIF that can be embedded in docs and the quickstart modal. Deliverables must include Figma frames, annotated exportable PNGs for docs, alt-copy for accessibility, and localization-ready copy strings (EN/DE/FR/JP).

Scope: Visual explorations (3 variants) + final polished assets. Annotations to explain inputs (expected QPS, p95 latency target, burst buffer), result interpretation (throughput, estimated monthly cost, recommended GPU profile), and fallback behavior when capacity limits are hit. Also produce a short 10–15 second looped GIF showing autoscale from baseline -> surge -> scaled -> cooldown with cost/latency overlays. Provide engineering handoff notes for the estimator API (input schema + telemetry) and screenshot variants for light/dark themes.

Constraints: Use existing Redwood UI tokens and icons. Keep pixel parity with Console 2026 style guide. Animated GIF must be <2s per loop and under 1MB if possible for docs performance. All strings must be provided as discrete keys for localization.

Success metric: PM and Eng can ship the quickstart modal without additional design clarifications; doc maintainers accept assets and localized strings on first pass.
